title: Why Betting Everything on One Stock Will Ruin You | Jungle Money Tales Ep 7 #shorts
description: Kiko bets his entire winter supply of nuts on a single miracle tree, only for a sudden blight to destroy everything. Learn why broad index funds and diversification beat stock picking every single time.
twist: Lakshmi's fund lost several trees to the blight, but generated more total nuts than ever because the surviving trees thrived.
viewer_question: Do you pick single stocks or buy index funds? Tell us below!

beat_sheet.hook: Stop scrolling: putting every nut in one single tree destroyed this shiba.
beat_sheet.trait_conflict: Kiko's reckless impatience and desire for big returns collides with single-stock concentration risk.
beat_sheet.want_and_stake: Kiko wants to triple his winter food, but risks total starvation if his chosen tree dies.
beat_sheet.clock: Two days before winter food is locked in the storehouse.
beat_sheet.money_in_numbers: 100 nuts in 1 tree promised to become 300, vs 100 nuts spread across 100 trees.
beat_sheet.the_trick: Gulab convinces Kiko to bet all his savings on a single miracle tree instead of diversifying.
beat_sheet.warning_ignored: Lakshmi and Shweta warn Kiko to spread his nuts, but Kiko laughs off small steady growth.
beat_sheet.lowest_point: The miracle tree rots from blight, Kiko borrows 50 nuts for a second tree which lightning destroys, leaving him with 0 food and 50 debt.
beat_sheet.wit_turn: Shweta shares the Panchatantra fable of the mouse with a hundred holes, inspiring Kiko to join the broad Forest Fund.
beat_sheet.moral: The mouse with one hole is dinner; the mouse with a hundred holes goes free.
beat_sheet.money_lesson: Index funds spread risk across entire markets so no single company collapse ruins your financial future.
beat_sheet.clue: Lakshmi's Forest Fund sign shows steady green growth across hundreds of tiny tree slices.
beat_sheet.cliffhanger: Next: a freezing night strips the whole forest of leaves.

moral: The mouse with one hole is dinner; the mouse with a hundred holes goes free.
recap: Kiko lost all his winter nuts on a single tree until Lakshmi showed him how index funds spread risk safely.
cliffhanger: Next: a freezing night strips the whole forest of leaves.

cast.name: Kiko
cast.role: small, sharp, cheeky shiba who notices details and loves a clever test, but sometimes bets too big
cast.catchphrase: Hmm, that does not add up.
cast.behaviour: trots, tilts his head, pounces on a clue, shows shock with wide eyes

cast.name: Gulab
cast.role: charming trader who runs the Trading Post, always smiling, everybody trusts him (hidden mastermind, never reveal before the reveal episode)
cast.behaviour: calm, smooth, always smiling, walks slowly, never raises his voice, filmed from a friendly eye-level angle until the reveal
cast.catchphrase: Trust is the best currency, my friend.

cast.name: Lakshmi
cast.role: kind honest cow, saves a little every day, protects the young
cast.behaviour: calm, gentle, eats while she talks, nods, never in a hurry

shots.title: The Creeping Blight
shots.narration: Stop scrolling: betting everything on one single tree destroyed this shiba. A black blight creeps through the orchard, darkening Kiko's leaves.
shots.visual: A dark black blight creeps over leaves as Kiko watches in horror inside a dim forest.

shots.title: The Single Miracle Bet
shots.narration: Two days before winter, Kiko watched his hundred nuts rot. He had put every berry into one single miracle oak.
shots.visual: Kiko stands beside a wooden sign showing his single miracle tree investment.

shots.title: Gulab's Pitch
shots.narration: Gulab had smiled smoothly yesterday. "Trust me, little friend, this miracle tree will triple your hundred nuts by winter!"
shots.visual: Gulab smiles silkily as he sells the miracle tree concept to Kiko in autumn light.

shots.title: Lakshmi's Warning
shots.narration: Lakshmi the cow had warned him at the storehouse. "Come here, little one. Spread your nuts across many trees instead."
shots.visual: Lakshmi points gently toward her Forest Fund board showing many small trees.

shots.title: Kiko Rejects Safety
shots.narration: Kiko had laughed and waved her away. "Hmm, that does not add up! Why pick small bushes over one miracle?"
shots.visual: Kiko laughs cheekily at Lakshmi, dismissing her safe fund advice.

shots.title: Total Ruin of Tree One
shots.narration: Now the blight swallowed his miracle tree completely. Every single nut turned to grey ash before his wide eyes.
shots.visual: Kiko stares in total despair as the black blight turns his miracle tree to dust.

shots.title: Shweta's Question
shots.narration: Wise Shweta stepped forward slowly. "Ask the question first, Kiko. Will you put your final winter food into another gamble?"
shots.visual: Wise Shweta stands tall in front of Kiko, asking a sharp measured question.

shots.title: Doubling Down on Debt
shots.narration: Desperate, Kiko ignored her warning. He borrowed fifty nuts and bought a single replacement pine, betting everything once more.
shots.visual: Kiko runs through rain to Gulab to borrow money for a replacement tree.

shots.title: Lightning Strikes Again
shots.narration: That very night, a heavy storm struck the valley. Lightning shattered Kiko's single pine, burning his borrowed money away.
shots.visual: A flash of lightning destroys Kiko's single replacement pine tree.

shots.title: The Lowest Point
shots.narration: And then the worst was still coming. Kiko stood broke, frozen in the rain, owing fifty nuts with no food left.
shots.visual: Kiko sits drenched in rain, completely broke and carrying heavy debt.

shots.title: Lakshmi's Fund Survives
shots.narration: Yet Lakshmi remained calm. Her Forest Fund owned tiny slices of five hundred trees. A few died, but most flourished.
shots.visual: Lakshmi stands beside her sign showing her diversified fund thriving despite the storm.

shots.title: The Mouse Tale
shots.narration: Shweta turned to Kiko in the rain. "Remember the old tale of the mouse with a hundred escape holes."
shots.visual: Shweta walks up to Kiko in misty morning light, ready to impart ancient wisdom.

shots.title: The Invitation
shots.narration: Lakshmi offered her bowl gently. "Join our broad Forest Fund, Kiko. Spread your risk so no single storm destroys you."
shots.visual: Lakshmi offers a bowl of mixed nuts, inviting Kiko into the broad Forest Fund.

shots.title: Buying the Forest
shots.narration: Kiko gave his last five nuts to the fund. He stopped picking single miracle trees and bought the whole valley instead.
shots.visual: Kiko hands his remaining small nuts into Lakshmi's collective fund basket.

shots.title: Winter Abundance
shots.narration: Months passed and winter arrived. While five trees withered in cold winds, hundreds of others dropped fresh nuts for everyone.
shots.visual: Lakshmi and Kiko stand in a lush orchard dropping fresh nuts across the meadow.

shots.title: The Contrast
shots.narration: Gulab's single miracle tree stood barren, while Lakshmi handed Kiko his steady share of winter berries from the whole forest.
shots.visual: Gulab looks glum beside his dead miracle tree while Lakshmi gives Kiko his share.

shots.title: Safe Savings
shots.narration: Kiko smiled as his savings grew safely. Spreading small nuts across many trees protected his food from any sudden blight.
shots.visual: Kiko celebrates beside his pile of safe nuts in warm golden sunlight.

shots.title: The Moral
shots.narration: Old Shweta nodded wisely. "The mouse with one hole is dinner; the mouse with a hundred holes goes free."
shots.visual: Wise Shweta delivers the ancient proverb under the golden sky.

shots.title: The Money Lesson
shots.narration: The money lesson: index funds diversify your money. Single stocks can fail. For example, five hundred companies protect your thousand dollars.
shots.visual: Lakshmi explains index funds clearly to Kiko and Shweta.

shots.title: Outro & Next Teaser
shots.narration: Do you pick single stocks or buy index funds? Tell us below! Next: a freezing night strips the whole forest of leaves. Subscribe for the next money lesson! For education only, not financial advice. Investing involves risk, including loss of money.
shots.visual: Shweta addresses the audience directly as night falls over the green valley.

topic: Index funds and diversification: own a tiny slice of the whole forest instead of betting everything on one tree (broad, low-cost, no stock-picking, still not risk-free).
genre: a legend told by the old wolf
